chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad — all together from Ali ibn Asbat — from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying, and Egypt was mentioned, so he said: The Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Do not eat in its pottery, and do not wash your heads with its clay, for indeed it removes the sense of protective honour (ghayra) and begets the depravity of pimping (diayatha).

key_terms.الدياثة: Diayatha — the depravity of pimping or facilitating indecency; one who lacks ghayra; considered a grave moral failing
key_terms.الغيرة: Ghayra — protective jealousy, the sense of honour and guardianship over one's family from indecency; a virtue highly praised in Islamic ethics

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about using Egyptian pottery and clay according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) relays a prophetic statement in which the Prophet (SAWW) warns against using Egyptian pottery for eating or washing one's head with Egyptian clay. The Prophet explains that such use removes ghayra — the protective jealousy and sense of honour that guards family propriety — and causes diayatha, a term for the shamelessness and moral corruption of one who facilitates indecency in their household. This narration reflects concerns about environmental and material influences on moral character in early Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Asbaat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying, and Egypt was mentioned, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Neither eat in its pottery, nor wash your heads with its clay, for it would remove the honour and inherit the actions of a pimp’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and al-Husayn from Muhammad from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad all from Ali ibn Asbat who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

When a city (Egypt) was mentioned, the Holy Prophet, said, ‘You must not eat in its pottery bowls; do not wash your head with its clay because it takes away one’s courage (protective feeling) and causes one to become a pimp.’”
